jamie: Quick heads-up — I'm swapping offcall tomorrow morning. Leaving a short handoff and a couple of open questions about who to page for different failure modes.

diego: Appreciate it. Quick Q: if hosted API returns a spike in 5xxs but runtime infra (nodes + kube) looks healthy, who should get paged first — eng-runtime or eng-sre?

sophie: Short answer: runtime owns serving/model-level issues (model crashes, queues, KV cache fills, model OOMs). SRE owns infra (node failures, kube control plane, network). If it's 5xxs with model logs showing model exceptions -> runtime. If you see kube evictions/NodeNotReady -> eng-sre.

maria: Can we have a one-line rule to put in the handoff so the oncall knows who to page?

sophie: One-liner we use: "If metrics/logs point to model serving (stack traces, KV cache growth, model process restarts) -> page eng-runtime. If metrics point to infra (node/crashloop/kube events/network) -> page eng-sre. If unclear, page both with subject 'unclear-owner' and escalate via @escalation."

jamie: I'm adding a 3-step checklist to my handoff note so the person taking over can triage quickly: 
1) Check global error rate + per-model error rate in Console.
2) Check runtime logs + model process restarts.
3) Check infra events and node health.

sophie: Commands I run during triage (paste into terminal):
```
# runtime logs (last 15m)
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=redwood-serving --since=15m
# check recent node terminations (gcloud example)
gcloud compute instances list --filter='status:TERMINATED' --limit 10
```

diego: What's our working definition of an "incident" vs a minor degradation? We still get paged for every little blip.

sophie: Incident = sustained customer-facing SLA breach (e.g., >30% error rate vs baseline for >5 minutes), major region outage, or data-loss type failure. Degradation = perf regressions, small error bumps, increased latency that doesn't cross SLOs. Use incident-bot to declare; it will notify the incident channel and runbook.

oncall-bot: reminder — when handing off, include: open actions, active mitigations, current risks, and any temporary workarounds. See runbook: https://go/ri-oncall-runbook

jamie: Leaving these explicit notes in the handoff: 
- Risk: canary model "v2-small" shows memory pressure on p2 pool during long requests. Mitigation: autoscaler policy will add nodes but may be slow; fallback plan is to pin requests to v1-small if latency spikes.
- Paging path: If runtime alarm (error-rate/model-crash) -> page eng-runtime oncall. If infra alarm (node/cluster) -> page eng-sre. If noisy or still unclear after 10m -> page oncall-lead @maria.

diego: Sweet, clear enough. I'll take the swap tomorrow morning. Thanks for writing this up. :thumbsup:

sophie: One more note — if you see persistent token auth errors across customers, treat as high-priority and page both teams immediately; that tends to be a cross-layer issue.

jamie: Good call. Handing off now — I posted the checklists and risks to the handoff doc. Ping me if anything weird pops up.

maria: Thanks — acknowledged. If anyone wants, I can add the one-liners to the oncall checklist page later today.
